- Model consistently underestimates prices in early days of the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days.
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., 70+ → 72+), then corrects with a lagged downward bias.
- Mean reversion tendency: forecasts often overcorrect downward after recent highs, then drifts back up.
- Forecast bias is stronger in the middle of the 30-day window (days 15–25), where model tends to be 1–3% below true value.
- Late-period (days 25–30) forecasts are often too high, especially when true values show upward momentum or volatility.
- Model exhibits “lagged response” — reacts to recent price changes with delay, missing short-term reversals.
- When history includes a recent spike, model tends to overreact with a sharp upward forecast, then undercorrects later.
- Forecast error is more pronounced when true values show strong upward momentum (e.g., >70) — model underestimates the peak and overestimates the trough.
